title: 5 Financial Advisor Marketing Tips to Follow
summary: Financial advisor marketing matters for growing a client base. Learn the best marketing tips for advisors to expand their businesses.

## Tip #1: Lead With Value


Each element of your plan, from your[financial advisor bio](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/financial-advisor-bio-template) to your social media content to your email newsletter, should show clients evidence of what makes you different from your competitors. Audit your marketing materials to identify where you miss the mark in communicating your value. Replace vague wording with specific examples of how you can help clients succeed.


“A marketing strategy can single-handedly make or break an advisor’s practice,” said Dan Biagini, senior vice president and head of independent sales at American Equity. “A lot of advisors may think because they’re good at what they do, their phone will ring off the hook with people wanting to work with them. The reality is most advisors don’t know how to articulate their value to customers and often struggle to get in front of new prospects.”


If you’re unclear on your[value proposition](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/financial-advisor-value-proposition) , take inventory of your skills, experience and expertise. Evaluate your firm’s service offerings and niche, relative to your main competitors. Consider the benefits you deliver to your clients, how you meet their needs and where you exceed expectations. This assessment can provide a framework for developing a statement of value.

## Tip #2: Stay on Topic


Effective messaging communicates your value to prospects and it also speaks to a distinct need they have. Personalization can create an instant connection if you’re speaking directly to a prospect by name, and calling out a pain point or challenge they’re facing right now. This marketing tip is easiest to implement with[email campaigns](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/email-marketing-strategies-for-financial-advisors) , as you can tailor messages to individual prospects or prospect segments.


“Advisors must communicate about how they help their clients survive and thrive,” Biagini said.


There’s a time to share more about your professional background, including awards you’ve received, credentials you’ve earned or designations you hold. However, dropping those mentions into the conversation before you’ve built any type of rapport with a prospect can overshadow your core message.


Email nurture campaigns can help you break the ice with prospects slowly, so that by the time you’re ready to share a little more about your background, they’re invested and ready to listen. ## Tip #3: Share Intentionally


Use targeted, intentional sharing to optimize social media marketing campaigns so that the right prospects find your message, in the right places. Your[ideal client avatar](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/ideal-client-avatar) can shed light on where prospects spend their time online. Once you’ve identified the channels, create content that fits the preferred format of each platform and create a posting schedule that reflects when prospects typically visit each one.


This approach ensures that you aren’t just throwing your marketing efforts at the wall to see what sticks. That can lead to wasted time and poor results. Intentional content creation has another benefit if you can repurpose what you’ve created across multiple channels.


For example, your content creation process might look something like this:


### Publish a blog post ➡️ Use the post to create a script for a YouTube video ➡️ Choose one key takeaway to include in a short TikTok or Reel ➡️ Share a snippet of the post with a link back to your website in your next email newsletter


Nothing goes to waste and you create a more cohesive marketing message by sharing similar content across different platforms. A[social media calendar](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/social-media-calendar-for-financial-advisors) can help you track which content you share, coordinate your posts and avoid unintended repetition. You can also use your calendar to track key dates so you know when to publish timely content around topics like taxes or year-end financial planning.


## Tip #4: Balance Digital and Traditional Marketing


Develop parallel marketing plans to expand your reach online and offline. Consider the[digital platforms](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/digital-marketing-strategies-for-financial-advisors) your target prospects utilize most often as well as the analog marketing strategies they may be most receptive to. Distribute your promotion efforts among them in proportion to the expected ROI each one has the potential to generate.


“If you’re only running one marketing funnel, you are automatically hiding from a population of prospects who would never be in that funnel,” Biagini said. “For example, a prospect you get in front of via radio or a podcast typically is someone who would not attend an in-person workshop.”


For perspective, a typical financial advisor uses five different marketing channels, according to a 2026 Kitces report on how financial planners market their services.1 Among high-growth practices, commonly used tactics include client referrals (90%), centers of influence (71%), in-person networking (57%), social media (43%) and[search engine optimization](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/financial-advisor-seo) (43%).


Evaluating[client acquisition costs](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/client-acquisition-cost) and new revenue per client can help you determine which of your current marketing efforts yield the biggest payoff. You can then decide whether a higher investment in marketing is worth it to draw in more revenue and AUM from new clients.


## Tip #5: Tailor Your Services


Consider what you currently offer clients, then ask yourself where there might be room to improve or expand, possibly by[developing a new service offering](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/how-to-develop-a-new-service-offering) . Tailor the offering to the clients you already have, the ones you hope to attract or both, if possible. Ask your current clients where the gaps exist in your services and use that as a guide to determine how to best add value.


“Advisors need to be thinking about how to add services to their practice that help them become a customer’s personal CFO and not just a stock trader or money manager,” Biagini said.


For example, estate planning services are something advised clients increasingly expect their advisors to offer. A 2026 report from Trust & Will found that 61% of Americans say financial advisors should offer estate planning as part of their services.2 Your target prospects may feel the same or be interested in working with an advisor who can assist with legacy planning, college planning or something entirely different than the usual scope of advice.


Review your offerings through the eyes of clients and consider where you could expand, either with brand-new services or complementary ones that are related to something you already advise on. If you need to obtain a credential, certification or license, such as a[life insurance license](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/how-to-get-life-insurance-license) , build that into your timeline for developing the offer.
